title: Booker Ervin from Denison, Texas
summary: On Buster Smith's tip he hires Booker Ervin, a big-toned Dallas-style tenor who stayed a couple of years.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Now, let's go on. You had Booker Ervin in the band?

Yeah. Now Booker Ervin is Dallas. You talk about this Dallas style, there's something about it. Somebody opened my eyes--when I had that incident in 1939 about Amos Woodruff--so I got to talking and needed a sax man. I was asked what kind of man and I said I definitely wanted somebody that can improvise and still have a good tone and some soul. I don't want somebody just blowing notes.
And so, we were in Dallas, Texas and Buster Bailey--I mean Buster Smith--who had been with Basie a long time, and Buster incidentally had done a lot of work for me and so

he says there's a youngster Ernie, who will fit, and I don't know what you're talking about, in Denison, Texas. So I got hold of Booker and he joined the band, and Booker just turned out to have that style that so many of them had coming from that area, a great big tone--if you remember Herschel Evans.
And swing right on out and was very good on all of them, but I used him on baritone and tenor, and certainly tenor was his main instrument.
How long did Booker stay with you?
I imagine at least a couple of years.
